races.name: bet365 Handicap

runners_data.name: Calico Blue
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to expected strong pace but 287-day absence is a significant fitness concern
runners_data.comment: Absent since last July but twice looked good at Chester last summer; handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Chester (6f, good) last June on second start and comfortably followed up in novice there (6f, good) the following month; absent since and this handicap debut is a much tougher test of his credentials, but he's a bright prospect and it remains to be seen where his limitations lie.

runners_data.name: Old Is Gold
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid form on similar going but long absence and gelding operation add question marks
runners_data.comment: Midfield at York last August but close third in nursery at Glorious Goodwood previously
runners_data.spotlight: Midfield in big-field nursery at York's Ebor meeting (6f, good to firm) last August when last seen; gelded since; however, close third in a nursery at Glorious Goodwood (6f, good to soft) previously, showing good pace, and he's in the picture on that form; also effective on good/good to firm.

runners_data.name: One And Gone
runners_data.note: Prominent style puts him in the danger zone where traffic problems are most likely to occur
runners_data.comment: Some good AW handicap form but he's probably vulnerable against unexposed types
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up on debut at Ripon (6f, good) last August and won Kempton novice (6f, AW) in November on fourth start; some good AW handicap efforts since but not last time and he's probably vulnerable against unexposed types.

runners_data.name: Atticum
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose 5f specialist profile fits this trip perfectly after impressive Yarmouth victory
runners_data.comment: Impressed at Yarmouth when last seen & could have plenty more to offer; yard in good form
runners_data.spotlight: Built upon last September's debut (5f, AW) to go close at Nottingham (5f, good to soft), then went one better at Yarmouth (5f, good to soft) in October when last seen; he could do with breaking more professionally but he impressed last time and could have plenty more to offer; yard in good form.

runners_data.name: Hypnotised
runners_data.note: Prominent style but trainer's poor 14-day record and 215-day break raise serious fitness doubts
runners_data.comment: Won AW maiden last September; attractive pedigree and could take higher order still
runners_data.spotlight: Built upon the promise of his first two starts (6f, good/AW) when readily winning a Southwell maiden (5f, AW) at odds-on last September; his attractive pedigree provides optimism that he can take higher order still.

runners_data.name: Black Star Boy
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who could benefit if allowed soft fractions but tendency to pull hard is concerning
runners_data.comment: Won in good style at Newbury last September; well bred and has potential off opening mark
runners_data.spotlight: Won with something to spare at Newbury (6f, good to soft) last September on second start then pulled hard when mid-division in Listed race at York (6f, good); gelded since, which may settle him down, and this well-bred sort has potential off his opening mark.

runners_data.name: Sir Alfie
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with recent race fitness advantage having run just 8 days ago
runners_data.comment: Below par on final two starts last term and same story on recent reappearance at Newmarket
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins last summer for Ger Lyons but down the field in Listed races last autumn on both starts for Charles Byrnes and soundly beaten in a handicap at Newmarket last Thursday on his stable/seasonal debut; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Ambishio
runners_data.note: Front-runner with recent AW form but question marks over turf effectiveness after poor 2023 season
runners_data.comment: Progressive on AW this year, having been gelded; thereabouts if return to turf is no issue
runners_data.spotlight: 0-5 last year, all on turf, but he showed promise and won a handicap at Southwell (5f, AW) in January on his first run since being gelded; close second at Southwell (5f, AW) a fortnight ago and could be thereabouts if the return to grass isn't an issue.

runners_data.name: Underwriter
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who historically fades in finish, making him vulnerable in a sustained gallop
runners_data.comment: 6f maiden/novice wins last year; returns having been gelded; could be suited by drop to 5f
runners_data.spotlight: Won maiden/novice races at Ayr (6f, good to firm/good) last season on two of his first three starts; came up short in Group/sales races otherwise but reappears having been gelded and he could prove well suited by this first crack at 5f; interesting on handicap debut, especially if backed.

races.paceDynamic: Black Star Boy and Ambishio will establish the early tempo, with Black Star Boy's front-running style likely to dictate terms from the rail. Four horses (Old Is Gold, One And Gone, Sir Alfie, Hypnotised) wanting prominent positions creates congestion through the first two furlongs before settling. The sustained gallop over 5f on good ground will expose stamina limitations, particularly as the pace intensifies approaching the final furlong. This honest tempo strongly favours hold-up horses like Calico Blue and Atticum who can produce late kicks when the early pace takes its toll.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Black Star Boy and Ambishio maintain strong early fractions through halfway
scenarios.body: The sustained pace burns out the prominent pack, creating perfect conditions for closers to sweep past tired leaders in the final furlong. Calico Blue and Atticum benefit most from this tactical setup with their proven finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent pressure cooker
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent runners (Old Is Gold, Sir Alfie, One And Gone, Hypnotised) engage in early scrimmaging behind the leaders
scenarios.body: The mid-pack becomes a tactical mess with horses getting shuffled back or forced wide, allowing one prominent runner to get first run. Sir Alfie or Old Is Gold can capitalize on superior class when others are still organizing their challenges.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner steals it
scenarios.trigger: If Black Star Boy gets an uncontested lead while Ambishio settles just off the pace
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows Black Star Boy to control fractions and kick clear, while the prominent horses react too late to the acceleration. His Newbury win suggests he has the tactical speed to exploit soft fractions over this shorter trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapse carnage
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too fast early while the prominent quartet also engages aggressively
scenarios.body: The entire front half of the field comes back dramatically in the final furlong, creating opportunities for any horse with late pace. Even lesser-fancied runners like Underwriter could benefit if positioned perfectly for the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Black Star Boy and Ambishio could set unsustainable fractions if they engage in early speed duel
Traffic problems likely at 2f out when four prominent runners try to improve position simultaneously
Calico Blue's 287-day absence could blunt his finishing kick despite ideal tactical setup
Jamie Spencer on Underwriter may try to overcome his mount's finishing limitations with aggressive tactics
Recent race fitness gives Sir Alfie and Ambishio significant advantages over long-absent rivals

races.name: bet365 Esher Cup Handicap

runners_data.name: Organise
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with Gosden yard in excellent form, just 13 days since comfortable Yarmouth win suggests sharp preparation
runners_data.comment: 2-2 and could have lots more left in the tank for last year's winning yard; key player
runners_data.spotlight: Impressive on debut at Southwell (7f, AW) last November and made it 2-2 in Yarmouth novice (1m, good) on recent reappearance; his inexperience was still evident last time and this well-bred colt could have lots more left in the tank for last year's winning yard; key player on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Nobody Knows
runners_data.note: Pure hold-up merchant under Moore, needs strong pace and may struggle if gallop is only moderate given 38-day absence
runners_data.comment: 2-2, cosily as favourite each time; Ryan Moore booked; has potential off opening mark
runners_data.spotlight: Well-backed winner at Ayr (7f, soft) last September on sole 2yo start and made it 2-2 in Wolverhampton novice (8.6f, AW) last month, again doing it cosily; has potential off his opening mark and the booking of Ryan Moore is a bonus.

runners_data.name: Laureate Crown
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been gelded since last season, 32 days off and needs significant pace collapse to be effective
runners_data.comment: Reappearance win came in small field but the form has been franked by the clear runner-up
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't really kick on last year after winning at Ascot (7f, good to firm) on debut but he reappeared at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) last month having been gelded and defied a slow start to win by half a length; it was a small field but the clear runner-up finished second in a good handicap at Newmarket subsequently and this fellow may well be in the mix up 6lb.

runners_data.name: Look To The Stars
runners_data.note: Godolphin front-runner returning after 195 days off, historical course winner but lengthy absence raises fitness doubts

runners_data.name: Breathe Easy
runners_data.comment: Narrow win in small field on handicap debut; in good hands to continue to progress
runners_data.spotlight: All four starts on AW; won at Kempton (7f) in January on third run and narrowly followed up in four-runner handicap at Southwell (1m); further improvement is necessary but he's in good hands to continue to progress.

runners_data.name: Suspended Sentence
runners_data.note: Another hold-up performer who won over course and distance previously, but 207-day layoff creates stamina questions at this stage
runners_data.comment: Won small-field nursery over C&D last September but makes reappearance off 13lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Won Ripon novice (1m, good to firm) last August on third start then followed up in four-runner nursery over this C&D (soft); creditable Listed fourth in France (1m, soft) in September but returns to a handicap off a mark 13lb higher than for his course win; further improvement needed.

runners_data.name: Goodwood Galaxy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying top weight after Group 2 Vintage Stakes fourth, 217-day break suggests needs this run badly
runners_data.comment: Good fourth in Group 2 at Goodwood last July but has to prove he can cut it off this mark
runners_data.spotlight: Won on debut at Salisbury (7f, good to firm) last June and kept on for fourth in Group 2 Vintage Stakes at Goodwood (7f, good) next time; ran okay in quality conditions race at Newbury (1m, good to soft) in September when last seen but he needs to prove he can cut it off this lofty mark.

runners_data.name: Capall Rasa
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who prefers all-weather surfaces, switching back to turf after AW wins creates surface adaptation concerns
runners_data.comment: Best 2yo form came on AW but did it easily last time and he's not discounted back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Improved upon first two runs (both on turf) to win at Southwell (7f, AW) last October, and followed up on handicap debut there (1m, AW); had just three rivals to beat last time and he's 12lb higher today with something to prove on turf, but is not discounted given the ease of that last win.

races.paceDynamic: Organise and Look To The Stars will ensure a strong gallop from the outset, with Breathe Easy (non-runner) removing one pace angle but still leaving sufficient early speed. The dual front-runners will stretch the field over this testing mile, creating a searching examination of stamina. Hold-up horses Nobody Knows, Laureate Crown, Suspended Sentence, Goodwood Galaxy and Capall Rasa will need the pace to collapse to be effective. This race shape heavily favours prominent racers and those with proven stamina at the trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Strong Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If Organise and Look To The Stars maintain a relentless pace throughout
scenarios.body: The strong early gallop continues and tests the stamina of all runners, with only the most resolute stayers surviving the final furlong. Hold-up horses find insufficient pace collapse to mount their customary late charges.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners tie up badly in the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: Look To The Stars and Organise pay for their early exertions, allowing the hold-up brigade to sweep past in the closing stages. The race becomes a sprint finish between fresh closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners are restrained early creating a moderate pace
scenarios.body: The anticipated strong gallop fails to materialise as jockeys play a waiting game, turning this into a tactical affair. Those with the most natural speed from off the pace will benefit from the sprint finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Solo Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner gets an uncontested lead while the other is held up
scenarios.body: Either Organise or Look To The Stars secures easy fractions alone in front while their main pace rival tracks behind. The solo leader builds an unassailable advantage through controlled sectionals.

watchPoints.text: Look To The Stars showing any signs of rustiness early given the 195-day absence could eliminate a key pace angle
Nobody Knows and Goodwood Galaxy both need the front-runners to go too fast early to set up their hold-up tactics
Organise's behaviour at the start and early pace judgement from Doyle will largely determine how this race unfolds
The ground remaining genuinely good rather than easing, as several hold-up horses have better form on softer surfaces
Jockey tactics on Look To The Stars - whether Buick sends him forward immediately or attempts to track the pace

races.name: bet365 Gordon Richards Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Saddadd
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 212-day break but showed good recent form before the layoff and Ray Dawson excels with this running style.

runners_data.name: King Of Cities
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore booking suggests strong chances but needs pace collapse to be effective from his hold-up position.

runners_data.name: Muddy Mooy
runners_data.note: Prominent style perfectly suits this race shape and recent Kempton third ties in well with Devil's Advocate's form.
runners_data.comment: Ran well at Kempton on reappearance but isn't sure to progress further back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Has gained both wins on AW and she did well to finish third, in difficult circumstances, at Kempton (1m2f Listed) on reappearance; ties in with Devil's Advocate on that bare form but isn't guaranteed to find the required further improvement back on turf.

runners_data.name: Almeric
runners_data.note: Highest official rating (OR 117) but 188-day absence is concerning despite excellent record when fresh.

runners_data.name: Devil's Advocate
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who can control the race tempo and William Buick partnership adds tactical nous.

races.paceDynamic: Devil's Advocate will take the field along from the front with Muddy Mooy sitting just behind in the prominent position, creating a controlled tempo in this small Group 3 field. The three hold-up horses (Saddadd, King Of Cities, and Almeric) will settle towards the rear, relying on the tactical pace to set up their finishing kicks. With no genuine speed pressure on Devil's Advocate early, he can dictate fractions and potentially steal a march turning for home. This race shape strongly favors the prominent runners who can track the leader and strike first, as the hold-up horses may find themselves with too much to do if the pace becomes tactical.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Devil's Advocate and Muddy Mooy are allowed to control the tempo without early pressure.
scenarios.body: Devil's Advocate can dictate ideal fractions and kick clear turning for home, while Muddy Mooy tracks him perfectly to strike in the straight. The hold-up trio get caught flat-footed by the change of pace and can't reel in the prominent pair.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Quality
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely slow and the race becomes a sprint from the 3f pole.
scenarios.body: Almeric and King Of Cities benefit from their superior class ratings (OR 117/110) as the race becomes a pure test of acceleration. The prominent pair go too early and get swamped by the finishing kick of the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Dawson Timing On Saddadd
scenarios.trigger: If Ray Dawson can find the perfect stalking position and time his challenge to perfection.
scenarios.body: Saddadd gets the ideal trip tracking the leaders before unleashing a devastating late run that catches the prominent pair and outfinishes the other hold-up horses. His recent good form (32113-) suggests he's ready to strike.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Mess Helps Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the small field creates positioning problems and several horses get inconvenienced in running.
scenarios.body: The race becomes scrappy with horses getting blocked or forced wide, allowing one of the lesser-rated horses to benefit from a clear passage. Muddy Mooy's prominent style helps her avoid trouble while others struggle for racing room.

watchPoints.text: If Devil's Advocate gets a soft lead through the first half-mile, he becomes very dangerous as he can control the finish.
Watch Almeric in the preliminaries after his 188-day break - any signs of rustiness would be significant.
Muddy Mooy's positioning behind Devil's Advocate early will be crucial - she needs to track him closely.
If King Of Cities gets too far back early, Ryan Moore may struggle to make up the ground in this small field.
Ray Dawson's timing on Saddadd will be critical - he needs to avoid getting caught behind horses in the straight.

races.name: bet365 Mile (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Zeus Olympios
runners_data.note: Unbeaten front-runner returning after 210 days but Ryan Moore's booking and progressive profile suggest he's ready to fire fresh.
runners_data.comment: Highly progressive in his first season and still unbeaten (4-4); remains one to follow
runners_data.spotlight: Highly progressive in his first campaign last year and still unbeaten (4-4); won going away from Opera Ballo in Group 2 at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) on final start; remains one to follow and has the makings of a Group 1 colt this term; commands respect.

runners_data.name: Field Of Gold
runners_data.note: Supreme hold-up performer whose last two runs had valid excuses, and the class edge on ratings may prove decisive if getting the right setup.
runners_data.comment: Impressive in Irish 2,000 Guineas and SJP prior to excusable defeats; sets the standard
runners_data.spotlight: Very progressive until having plausible excuses in the Sussex Stakes (found to be lame) and QEII (draw to some extent) in last two appearances; impressive wins in the Irish 2,000 Guineas and St James's Palace Stakes make him the one to beat, provided he's back in similar form.

runners_data.name: Opera Ballo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with Group 1 form at Meydan who could benefit from tracking Zeus Olympios without making the running himself.
runners_data.comment: Group 1 winner at Meydan last time; no match for Zeus Olympios in last domestic start
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive colt who readily bagged Group 1 honours at Meydan (1m1f, good) three months ago, taking record to 6-8; however, appears to need further improvement to defy 5lb penalty and was no match for Zeus Olympios in last domestic outing.

runners_data.name: Never So Brave
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning after 188 days but his hat-trick last season including Group 1 success shows he has the necessary class.
runners_data.comment: Did very well last season for new yard; not disgraced in QEII; may rate higher still
runners_data.spotlight: Did very well (3-5) last season for new stable, completing a notable summer hat-trick (7f/1m, good to firm) that culminated in Group 1 success at York; not disgraced from unfavourable draw in the QEII on final outing; may rate higher still and looks likely to go well.

runners_data.name: Dancing Gemini
runners_data.note: Another hold-up horse whose form tailed off in 2025, and the poor recent trainer record (1/7) adds further concern.
runners_data.comment: Won this race last year but is facing a slightly stiffer assignment in this field
runners_data.spotlight: Below best in three of his last four outings in 2025 but commenced the campaign splendidly, winning twice (including in this race) then going close in the Group 1 Lockinge; while today may be a good time to catch him, he faces a slightly stiffer assignment in this field.

runners_data.name: Cicero's Gift
runners_data.note: Dual course winner but may be flattered by rating and faces a tactical disadvantage from his hold-up style in this pace setup.
runners_data.comment: Needs to prove he can back up the form of his 100-1 win in the Group 1 QEII
runners_data.spotlight: Dual C&D winner who finished third in this race last year; returns to Sandown but may be flattered by his new rating, having been perhaps helped by the draw when registering a 100-1 success in the Group 1 QEII at Ascot (good) on last appearance; needs to prove he can back up that form.

races.paceDynamic: Zeus Olympios will take them along from the front with his confirmed leading style, likely setting a measured tempo given the lack of other natural pace in this 6-runner field. Field Of Gold, Opera Ballo, Never So Brave, Dancing Gemini and Cicero's Gift all possess hold-up or prominent tendencies, meaning they'll be content to sit behind the leader. With limited early pressure on Zeus Olympios, he can dictate fractions and potentially steal a march turning for home. This tactical setup strongly favours the front-runner and any horse capable of tracking close, as the hold-up brigade may find themselves with too much to do in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zeus Dominates Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Zeus Olympios gets an easy lead without early pressure from the field.
scenarios.body: He can control the tempo completely and use his unbeaten record to kick clear when it matters, making the closers' task near-impossible. The lack of pace pressure plays directly into his hands as the proven front-runner.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Kick Catches Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Zeus Olympios goes too slow early and one of the hold-up horses produces a telling late surge.
scenarios.body: Field Of Gold or Never So Brave could time their challenge perfectly to reel in a tiring leader in the final furlong. Their superior ratings suggest they have the class edge if getting the right tactical setup.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Opera Ballo or another prominent runner sits closer to Zeus Olympios than expected.
scenarios.body: A horse tracking the leader can strike at the perfect moment before the hold-up horses get organised, benefiting from race position without doing the donkey work. Opera Ballo's Group 1 form suggests he has the quality to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Shuffle
scenarios.trigger: If Zeus Olympios stops quickly and creates a messy finish where positioning becomes crucial.
scenarios.body: The race could become a lottery with multiple horses having chances in a blanket finish, favouring whoever gets the clearest run. This scenario requires the favourite to underperform significantly based on his unbeaten record.

watchPoints.text: Zeus Olympios breaks slowly or gets headed early - his whole tactical advantage disappears if he can't establish the lead cleanly.
Field Of Gold's fitness after 188 days off - any signs of needing the run could be costly given his hold-up style needs peak sharpness.
How close Opera Ballo positions himself to Zeus Olympios in the early stages - sitting closer than usual could be key to his chances.
The pace through the first half-mile - if Zeus Olympios goes too steady, it sets up perfectly for the closers with superior ratings.
Never So Brave's jumping from the stalls after his long break - hold-up horses can't afford to be slowly away in small fields.

races.name: bet365 Classic Trial (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Raaheeb
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with outstanding pedigree but major concern over 231-day layoff affecting race sharpness
runners_data.comment: Smartly bred; justified favouritism at Ascot in sole 2yo outing; bright prospect
runners_data.spotlight: Smartly bred, being a brother to Baaeed and Hukum; duly showed strong promise in justifying favouritism at Ascot (7f, soft) in sole 2yo outing; held a Royal Lodge entry at the time and currently holds three major entries, including the Derby; should be suited by middle distances; bright prospect.

runners_data.name: Al Zanati
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits race shape perfectly with Charlie Appleby's excellent strike rate and good recent Group 3 AW form
runners_data.comment: AW Group 3 win in France took his record to 2-3; further progress may materialise
runners_data.spotlight: Dubawi colt who got up in the final strides to win 1m1f AW Group 3 at Chantilly on final 2yo start, taking record to 2-3; looks likely to be well suited by going up further in distance; doesn't have a Derby entry but further progress may materialise.

runners_data.name: Action
runners_data.note: Natural leader who can control the tempo but Ryan Moore needs to judge the pace correctly to avoid being caught late
runners_data.comment: Ended progressive 2yo campaign with close second in the Group 1 Futurity; the form pick
runners_data.spotlight: Closely related to last year's Derby winner Lambourn and has his own Epsom aspirations, having ended a progressive 2yo campaign with close second to one of his stablemates in the Group 1 Futurity at Doncaster (1m, heavy); now goes in tongue-tie; the pick on the figures and may well rate higher still.

runners_data.name: Spyce
runners_data.note: Forward-going style ideal for this tactical contest with Alan King's 3/16 recent record providing confidence
runners_data.comment: Developing into a useful Flat performer for his esteemed dual-purpose trainer
runners_data.spotlight: Eye-catching second in the Convivial Maiden at York then went one better at Yarmouth and ran well in Group 3 at Newmarket (1m2f, good to firm) upped further in trip; developing into a useful Flat performer for his esteemed dual-purpose trainer.

runners_data.name: Winding Stream
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose recent 23-day gap gives fitness edge over most rivals returning from long breaks
runners_data.comment: AW form comprises a win and good second; faces a stiffer task at this level
runners_data.spotlight: Both starts on AW, scoring comfortably at Southwell (7f) as a 2yo then running well under a penalty at Kempton (1m); holds a Derby entry and may be suited by going up further in distance today but faces a stiff task at this level; bottom on bare figures.

runners_data.name: Wise Prince
runners_data.note: Hold-up style disadvantaged in small field but Gosden stable's 9/26 strike rate and Derby entries suggest hidden ability
runners_data.comment: Scored comfortably at Nottingham, looking the type who could become a Group colt
runners_data.spotlight: Ghaiyyath colt whose two major entries include the Derby; scored comfortably at Nottingham (1m, good to soft) in sole 2yo start, looking the type who'll be suited by middle distances and could develop into a Group performer this year; interesting contender.

runners_data.name: Oceans Four
runners_data.note: Class act but 216-day absence is major concern for a prominent runner needing to be sharp from the gate
runners_data.comment: Clear peak form when running well in the Solario; won French Group 3 next time
runners_data.spotlight: Narrowly bagged Group 3 honours at Chantilly (1m, soft) in September when last seen but still needs to prove he can repeat the clear peak form he appeared to show when going close at 25-1 in an exciting Solario at Sandown; gelding who has no major entries in the future.

races.paceDynamic: Action looks the confirmed front runner here with his forward-going style, while Al Zanati, Spyce, and Oceans Four will likely sit prominent positions behind him. With only seven runners and Action uncontested for the lead, he can dictate a sustainable tempo without pressure through the early stages. The race will develop into a tactical affair where those able to travel strongly into the straight will have the advantage. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can position handy and quicken, rather than hold-up horses who may struggle to make up ground in a small field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Action sets an uncontested lead and the pace stays steady
scenarios.body: Action can dictate terms throughout while Al Zanati and Spyce travel comfortably in behind, setting up a sprint finish that favours those with early tactical speed. The leaders will have too much in reserve for the hold-up horses to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Exposes Weakness
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens significantly from halfway due to multiple horses pressing Action
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will find out any fitness concerns after long layoffs and expose those lacking stamina at this trip. Oceans Four and Raaheeb, despite their class, may struggle with the tempo after extended breaks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Kick Decides
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes a tactical crawl with Action going very slowly early
scenarios.body: The race will turn into a sprint finish where raw speed and recent race fitness become crucial factors. Winding Stream's recent run gives him an edge while the long-absent runners may lack the sharp speed needed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-up Horse Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuine but not excessive, creating perfect stalking conditions
scenarios.body: Wise Prince can use his hold-up style to perfection while the prominent runners go too early in their effort to get competitive positions. His class and Derby entries suggest untapped ability.

watchPoints.text: Action's ability to sustain his gallop - if he weakens in the final furlong after setting the pace, Al Zanati is perfectly placed to pounce
Raaheeb's early positioning after 231 days off - if he's slowly away or takes time to find his stride, his class advantage diminishes significantly
Wise Prince's position turning for home - needs to be within striking distance despite his hold-up style to have any chance in this small field
The pace through the middle stages - if it becomes pedestrian, it transforms into a sprint finish favouring those with most recent race practice
Winding Stream's stamina at this 1m2f trip on debut at the distance - improvement needed from his 1m best to be competitive

races.name: bet365 "Wild Card" Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Felicitas
runners_data.comment: Oaks entry who won well at Lingfield (AW) in sole 2yo start; open to progress

runners_data.spotlight: 70,000gns yearling; Space Blues half-sister to five winners, notably California Dreamer (1m AW; Irish 1,000 Guineas runner-up; RPR 110); dam German Oaks winner; check the betting.

runners_data.spotlight: 110,000euros yearling; New Bay half-sister to five winners, notably Patrick Sarsfield (1m-1m2f including Group 3; RPR 114); one of two newcomers for her stable; market instructive.

runners_data.spotlight: Oaks entry who showed plenty of promise at Yarmouth (1m, good to soft) six months ago, beating all bar the market leader and faring best of the newcomers; enters the reckoning.

runners_data.spotlight: May do better in due course but is perhaps one for handicaps later on; bottom of this pack judged on her 2yo effort at Newbury (1m, soft).

runners_data.comment: Something to find on her October efforts but remains open to improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Something to find on her October efforts (1m) but remains open to improvement, being an Oaks entry who is related to several winners for her owner-breeder.

runners_data.name: Ribbon Of Sea
runners_data.comment: Scored at Wolverhampton on reappearance and is the type to rate higher still
runners_data.spotlight: Justified favouritism at Wolverhampton (9.5f, AW) on reappearance and is the type to rate higher still, being a Sea The Stars filly who cost 1,600,000gns as a yearling; respected.

races.name: Nordoff & Robbins Ozzy Osbourne Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Into The Light
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong finishing kick, Buick's big-race experience crucial, two solid AW performances suggest he's ready for turf step up
runners_data.comment: Godolphin colt; could prove to be on an advantageous mark for his first handicap start
runners_data.spotlight: Defied inexperience to win on debut at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) in February and again ran well when 3l second to a newcomer at Southwell (1m4f, AW) last month; his dam was a Listed winner and he could prove to be on an advantageous mark for his first handicap start.

runners_data.name: Lost Boys
runners_data.note: Long absence is a concern despite previous good to soft form, needs to prove he's maintained fitness after 209-day break
runners_data.comment: Promising over 1m on his three 2yo starts and bred to appreciate this longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Promising third last year on first two starts (1m, good/soft) then won Haydock maiden (1m, good to soft) in September; his dam was a 1m2f/1m4f winner and it seems likely that he'll improve for this step up in trip on handicap/seasonal debut; trainer won this in 2024.

runners_data.name: Colourband
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who must avoid going too fast early, recent Bath win on good ground confirms he handles the conditions
runners_data.comment: Returned to action with 4l win in recent Bath novice and he's respected on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up to exciting prospect at Kempton (1m, AW) in December on third and final 2yo start and returned to action with 4l win in Bath novice (1m2f, good) this month; likeable prospect who is respected on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: The Joker
runners_data.note: Best form over shorter trips raises stamina doubts, 175 days off the track means fitness is questionable despite trainer's 14-day record
runners_data.comment: 0-4 last year; bred to be suited by the longer trip but needs improvement off opening mark
runners_data.spotlight: Best of his four 2yo runs came when second here (7f, soft) in August, and he also showed promise on fast ground; bred to be suited by the step up in trip but he was headstrong on occasions last year, which is a concern, and improvement is needed off his opening mark.

runners_data.name: Bnaider
runners_data.note: Hold up style suits if pace is strong, but trainer's poor 14-day record and 182-day absence create fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: There's stamina in his pedigree; possible improver up in trip on this first handicap start
runners_data.spotlight: Took a step forward when up in trip and third at Newbury (1m, soft) last October on his third start; ran well on good ground on debut; there's stamina in his pedigree and he's a possible improver on this first handicap start.

runners_data.name: Magic Trip
runners_data.note: Strong closer who needs a true gallop to be effective, recent Kempton third suggests he's in good current form
runners_data.comment: Highly likely that he'll relish going beyond 1m for the first time; firmly in calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Won on debut at Bath (1m, good to soft) last September before 8l last of eight in Italian Group 3 (7.5f, good); reappeared with strong finish for third in Kempton novice (1m, AW) this month and his pedigree also suggests he'll relish the extra yardage today; firmly in calculations.

races.paceDynamic: Colourband is the sole confirmed front-runner in this small field and will control the tempo from the start. With Into The Light, Lost Boys, and The Joker all likely to settle prominently behind the leader, there's minimal early pressure expected. The pace will be measured through the early stages, setting up a sprint finish from the 3f pole where positions and stamina will matter. This sustainable gallop strongly favours horses with tactical speed who can quicken late, giving the prominent runners and strong finishers a significant edge over pure front-running tactics.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running Success
scenarios.trigger: If Colourband dictates an honest but manageable gallop without serious challenges
scenarios.body: The leader gets first run turning for home and holds off late challenges with James Doyle timing his kick perfectly. His recent Bath win shows he can control the pace and find extra when pressed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners get perfect stalking positions behind a steady pace
scenarios.body: Into The Light or Lost Boys can unleash superior finishing speed from ideal tracking spots 2-3 lengths off the leader. The Appleby runner especially has the class edge with William Buick's tactical nous.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Runner Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling through halfway allowing back markers to close
scenarios.body: Magic Trip and Bnaider can use their stamina reserves and closing kicks from the rear. The slow tempo negates the prominent runners' positional advantage entirely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If Colourband goes too slowly and bunches the field turning in
scenarios.body: The race becomes a 2f dash where pure speed trumps stamina and position. The Joker's 7f form suggests he has the raw pace for this finish.

watchPoints.text: Colourband's early fractions - if he goes too fast in the opening 4f he'll set up the race for the closers
Into The Light's turf debut - his AW form is solid but the surface switch at this trip length could expose stamina questions
Lost Boys' fitness after 209 days off - any early signs of rustiness will eliminate his chances in a tactical finish
The pace through the middle 4f - if it becomes pedestrian it will turn into a sprint finish favouring pure speed over stamina
Magic Trip's position turning in - he needs to be within 6 lengths of the leader with 3f to go to unleash his finishing kick
